summary: Aermotor lookout on the National Bison Range near St. Ignatius, built 1934 and gone by 1986; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Steel Aermotor tower with a frame cabin; also a wildlife observation point
facts.status_note: Tower and cabin gone by 1986 per firelookout.com and the CSKT list; the Montana list marks it Tower Gone

events.note: Built on the National Bison Range; a 1934 Missoulian item describes a crew erecting 60-foot towers, one planned for High Point

corrections.proposed: U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service (National Bison Range)
corrections.why: firelookout.com and the Montana page both name the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service for this site on the National Bison Range; the tribal list groups it with Flathead Reservation lookouts and names no agency for it.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1934 Missoulian item gives the planned towers as 60 feet; firelookout.com and the CSKT list give 65 feet for this tower. The record uses 65 feet (19.8 m).

firelookout.com and the Montana page name the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service; the tribal list places High Point among Flathead Reservation lookouts without naming an agency for it. The record follows the two sources that name an agency.

sources.title: Fire Lookouts
sources.publisher: Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes, Division of Fish, Wildlife, Recreation & Conservation

notes_for_editor: Brief access 'permission' is not supported by any source read, so it is omitted. Brief agency (CSKT) is corrected to USFWS on two sources; the CSKT list is still cited for the reservation context. Height conflict (60 vs 65 ft) is resolved in favour of the 65 ft sources. Staffing not found in the sources read. No source describes the site today. The 1968 survey description is quoted via the Montana page, not the NGS datasheet.
